description: Nos inspira la conexión entre el cielo y nuestro planeta, y el deseo de comprender nuestro lugar en el cosmos.
summary: NUT is a high-performance interactive web application developed for the visualization and geospatial analysis of 9 extreme terrestrial environments that replicate planetary conditions (Mars and the Moon). The platform integrates an interactive 3D globe synchronized with a dynamic 4-section technical datasheet, allowing users to quantitatively and qualitatively evaluate the similarity of each analog across 5 key scientific axes, alongside an interactive 3D rover exploration game mode where users analyze first-person planetary landscapes and classify their analogs.
details:
NUT is an interactive web platform designed for the exploration and analysis of nine extreme terrestrial environments that replicate the conditions of Mars and the Moon. The system works by integrating a 3D globe with a dynamic four-section technical datasheet: upon selecting a marker, the interface automatically displays coordinates, images, a similarity index based on five thematic axes (terrain, geology, thermal conditions, water resources, and wind activity), three validated scientific facts, and the corresponding mission target.

The benefits of the project include centralizing complex scientific information into a visual and intuitive tool that facilitates the study of natural laboratories for space exploration. Its expected impact is to serve as a didactic and advanced reference resource for students and researchers. For its development, the team utilized cutting-edge technologies such as HTML5, CSS3, modular JavaScript, and graphics libraries for three-dimensional rendering.

The project stands out for its creativity in merging geospatial visualization with normalized scientific databases, transforming navigation into a space mission experience. Throughout the process, the team considered critical factors such as the accuracy of geographic coordinates, the consistency of evaluation metrics, responsive design optimization, and interface fluidity.
